learningObjectives.text: Explain this episode: Who is struggling with the suitors in Ithaca?
Use the cited passage to explain: What makes the suitors a threat to the household?

main.author: Homer
main.locator: Book 1, the suitors’ feast; local text file lines 499-503 (physical file lines, not ancient verse numbers)
main.excerpt: Then the suitors came in and took their places on the benches and seats.3 Forthwith men servants poured water over their hands, maids went round with the bread-baskets, pages filled the mixing-bowls with wine and water, and they laid their hands upon the good things that were before them.
main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Odysseus is absent while suitors consume his household’s resources and press Penelope to marry. Athena encourages Telemachus to act. Homecoming begins as a crisis for those waiting at home, not just an adventure abroad.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “Then the suitors came in and took their places on the benches and seats.3 Forthwith men servants poured water over their hands, maids went round with the bread-baskets, pages filled the mixing-bowls with wine and water, and they laid their hands upon the good things that were before them.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: Homecoming matters because absence has already changed the home. The poem measures return not only in miles survived but in what remains to recover.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Read the household as part of the homecoming problem. The suitors’ behaviour shows what absence costs Penelope and Telemachus; the hero’s story is not confined to his own travels.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Carry this forward whenever Odysseus hides his name: identity and home are both being rebuilt.

quiz.prompt: Who is struggling with the suitors in Ithaca?
quiz.explanation: Telemachus. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: What makes the suitors a threat to the household?

choices.text: They consume its resources while pursuing Penelope.
They are guarding it against the returning king.
They have already escorted Odysseus home.
